001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.slf4j.spi;
002
003import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
004import org.slf4j.Logger;
005import org.slf4j.spi.LoggingEventBuilder;
006
007import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogConfig;
008import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEventLogger;
009import io.jstach.rainbowgum.RainbowGum;
010import io.jstach.rainbowgum.slf4j.ForwardingLogger;
011import io.jstach.rainbowgum.slf4j.WrappingLogger;
012import io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider;
013
014/**
015 * <strong>EXPERIMENTAL:</strong> this rainbowgum service provider allows wrapping slf4j
016 * loggers created from the logger factory. <em>This allows for custom filtering using the
017 * SLF4J api directly!</em>
018 * <p>
019 * If there are multiple registrations {@link #order()} and then {@link #name()} will be
020 * used to sort where the lower order number and name will
021 * {@linkplain #decorate(RainbowGum, DepthAwareLogger, int) decorate} first. See
022 * {@link RainbowGumServiceProvider} for details on how to register.
023 * <p>
024 * <strong>IMPORTANT implementation detail</strong> is that you should not call the SLF4J
025 * logger factory otherwise a stackoverflow or similar will happen.
026 *
027 * <h2>Writing a decorator</h2>
028 *
029 * Do not extend {@link org.slf4j.helpers.AbstractLogger} directly to implement the
030 * returned {@link Logger}: getting caller-info depth right means depending on that
031 * class's internal multi-arity dispatch shape, which is an unversioned SLF4J
032 * implementation detail rather than a contract, and is easy to get subtly wrong. Extend
033 * {@link AbstractFilteringLogger} instead - it owns and tests its own depth accounting so
034 * a decorator author never has to reason about stack frames.
035 * <p>
036 * A decorator that samples DEBUG level events and surfaces any {@link org.slf4j.Marker}
037 * as a key value (Rainbow Gum core has no built-in {@code Marker} support, so this is how
038 * a decorator can still make use of one):
039 *
040 * {@snippet class = "snippets.DecoratorExample" region = "decoratorExample" }
041 *
042 * Once built, register it like any other {@link RainbowGumServiceProvider}. If your
043 * application is modularized:
044 *
045 * {@snippet :
046 *
047 * provides io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider with com.mycompany.DecoratorExample;
048 *
049 * }
050 *
051 * @see ForwardingLogger
052 * @see RainbowGumServiceProvider
053 * @see AbstractFilteringLogger
054 */
055public abstract class LoggerDecoratorService implements RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator {
056
057        /**
058         * No arg constructor for service loader.
059         */
060        public LoggerDecoratorService() {
061
062        }
063
064        @Override
065        public final boolean configure(LogConfig config, Pass pass) {
066                config.serviceRegistry().put(LoggerDecoratorService.class, name(), this);
067                return true;
068        }
069
070        /**
071         * The name of the decorator and should be unique to avoid collisions.
072         * @return name.
073         */
074        public abstract String name();
075
076        /**
077         * Lowest integer value will decorate first which means the highest order found
078         * actually has the strongest influence on filtering since its returned logger is the
079         * one used.
080         * @return order.
081         */
082        public int order() {
083                return 0;
084        }
085
086        /**
087         * Decorate a logger. To not decorate simply return the previous logger.
088         * @param rainbowGum rainbow gum passed to the slf4j factory.
089         * @param previousLogger the previous logger in the chain.
090         * @param depth amount of times the logger has been wrapped. If the inputted logger is
091         * returned this number does not increase.
092         * @return decorated logger and if decorated ideally one that implements
093         * {@link WrappingLogger} so that caller info depth is retained.
094         */
095        public abstract Logger decorate(RainbowGum rainbowGum, DepthAwareLogger previousLogger, int depth);
096
097        /**
098         * Because wrapping can change the depth of the logger in the callstack this interface
099         * allows loggers to recreate themselves with the proper depth if they support it.
100         */
101        public interface DepthAwareLogger extends Logger {
102
103                /**
104                 * Will recreate the logger with desired depth.
105                 * @param depth new depth.
106                 * @return logger with new depth.
107                 */
108                public Logger withDepth(int depth);
109
110                /**
111                 * Will recreate the logger with desired depth if possible.
112                 * @param logger to check.
113                 * @param depth new depth.
114                 * @return logger with new depth or the same logger if not possible.
115                 */
116                public static Logger withDepth(Logger logger, int depth) {
117                        if (logger instanceof DepthAwareLogger da) {
118                                return da.withDepth(depth);
119                        }
120                        return logger;
121                }
122
123        }
124
125        /**
126         * Because wrapping can change the depth of the logger in the callstack this interface
127         * allows implementations to change the depth of the event builder.
128         */
129        public interface DepthAwareEventBuilder extends LoggingEventBuilder {
130
131                /**
132                 * Sets the depth of an event builder.
133                 * @param depth sets depth for caller info.
134                 * @return this.
135                 */
136                public LoggingEventBuilder setDepth(int depth);
137
138                /**
139                 * Will recreate the logger with desired depth if possible.
140                 * @param eventBuilder event builder to check.
141                 * @param depth new depth.
142                 * @return logger with new depth or the same logger if not possible.
143                 */
144                public static LoggingEventBuilder setDepth(LoggingEventBuilder eventBuilder, int depth) {
145                        if (eventBuilder instanceof DepthAwareEventBuilder da) {
146                                return da.setDepth(depth);
147                        }
148                        return eventBuilder;
149                }
150
151                /**
152                 * Redirects the output.
153                 * @param logger logger.
154                 * @return this.
155                 */
156                LoggingEventBuilder setLogger(LogEventLogger logger);
157
158                /**
159                 * The message set on this builder so far, if any. Plain
160                 * {@link LoggingEventBuilder} has no such accessor, which makes read-modify-write
161                 * use cases (e.g. prefixing) impossible without this.
162                 * @return message or null if not set.
163                 */
164                @Nullable String message();
165
166                /**
167                 * The message set on the builder so far, if possible.
168                 * @param eventBuilder event builder to check.
169                 * @return message, or null if not set or not a {@link DepthAwareEventBuilder}.
170                 */
171                public static @Nullable String message(LoggingEventBuilder eventBuilder) {
172                        if (eventBuilder instanceof DepthAwareEventBuilder da) {
173                                return da.message();
174                        }
175                        return null;
176                }
177
178        }
179
180}
